subject: SCIENCE
title: Materials Can Change
objective: Observe safe examples of changes from heating or cooling.
introduction: Milo watches an ice cube melt on a warm plate and water freeze in a freezer. What clues show a safe change from heat or cold?

vocabulary.definition: What something is made of, like wood or plastic.
To look closely and notice what happens.

items.prompt: Milo sees ice melt and water freeze. Which statement about heating and cooling is true?

options.text: Heating or cooling can cause physical changes; some are reversible and others are not.

items.explanation: Heating or cooling can change materials, but not every material melts and not every change can be undone. The observations show why we check the material and the cause.

items.prompt: Maxine puts an ice cube on a warm plate. Which example shows a change caused by heat?

options.text: Juice turns into ice pops in a freezer

items.explanation: Heat from the warm plate makes ice melt. Freezing happens when something cools, such as juice or wax in a freezer.

items.prompt: Milo reads four claims about changes. Which one is NOT true?
items.explanation: Not every material melts; some may soften, burn, break, or stay the same. Ice melting, water freezing, and wax softening are real observations.

items.prompt: Maxine leaves an ice cube in a warm room. What is she most likely to observe?
items.explanation: A warm room transfers heat to the ice, so it can melt into water. Heat does not turn ice into metal, fire, or wood.

items.prompt: With an adult nearby, Milo observes wax warming, ice melting, and a hot pan. Which change is safe and correct to observe?
items.explanation: Wax softening as it warms is a safe observation when an adult supervises. Hot objects should not be touched, and not every change reverses.
